kartice.naslov: GardenBench: A lightweight, daily evaluation of LLM capabilities
kartice.povzetek_sl:
arXiv:2610.23866v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce GardenBench, a benchmark with 11 test suites that evaluate the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) across a range of tasks. By systematically prompting LLMs with various lightweight queries, we document day-to-day changes in model performance, including run costs and times, that other benchmarks miss. This allows us to compare the accuracy and features of responses across model providers and versions. We account for daily variations in model accuracy, capturing both model progress and degradation, for instance, when a model is changed post-deployment or when a new model is released. We base our evaluation on general-use tasks and make our results publicly accessible via a live dashboard, diversifying existing approaches to LLM testing. Our main contribution is an innovative, lightweight, and inexpensive benchmark, designed to be consumer-facing and for everyday tasks.

viri.naslov: GardenBench: A lightweight, daily evaluation of LLM capabilities

kartice.naslov: Doing Less with More: A First-Principles Exploration of the Suitability of Agentic Computing over Alternative Architectural Choices
kartice.povzetek_sl:
arXiv:2610.23921v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: There is growing interest in automating business activities with Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) due to latter's seeming ease of use. Never has it been easier, or costlier, to do less with more. However, little is known about when agents are preferable to established alternatives such as local computation, Representational State Transfer (REST), the Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP), and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), particularly when development speed, performance, and operational cost are considered. We investigate this question using a controlled mathematical task that compares seven methods on a benchmark of 1,000 arithmetic expressions where semantics of operator precedence has to be preserved. We ran this setup across a native Function Calling baseline (Python library), REST, SOAP and MCP microservice architectures, direct responses from large language models (LLMs) using a Groq cloud API and five locally deployed Ollama models, and agentic systems in which five local LLMs invoke MCP tools. kartice.naslov: A Controlled LLM Workflow for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis of Risk Score Differences
kartice.povzetek_sl:
arXiv:2610.23962v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a controlled Large Language Model (LLM) workflow for explaining risk score differences using similar historical transactions. The workflow combines reference retrieval and contrastive SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) evidence with reference-based LLM reasoning and deterministic validation. Experiments on a test dataset show that the workflow produces more consistent, evidence-grounded and traceable diagnoses than the same LLM without structured workflow guidance.

kartice.naslov: What Social Media Teaches Us About Accumulative AI Risks
kartice.povzetek_sl:
arXiv:2610.24006v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Prominent AI safety discussions emphasize existential threats and catastrophic events, such as AI-enabled nuclear conflict or engineered biological outbreaks. This position paper argues that there is another type of AI risk that arises and accumulates from the widespread use of AI. Drawing on lessons from social media, we argue that safety assessments must also address accumulative harms that develop through repeated use, recurring decisions, and feedback across interconnected deployments. Repeated reassurance, selective exposure, recurring decision biases, and growing personal profiles may gradually narrow perspectives, weaken independent judgment, or enable exploitative influence without a single clearly harmful event. We advance the Trajectory Neglect Thesis: a focus on vivid catastrophic events and identifiable incidents risks overlooking less visible harms that accumulate through the widespread daily use of AI. Social media research motivates this position by showing how reciprocal media effects, social reinforcement, and individual susceptibility shape outcomes beyond individual encounters. kartice.naslov: Beyond Explicit Intent: Discovering and Shaping Artistic Intent through Human-AI Co-Creation
kartice.povzetek_sl:
arXiv:2610.24010v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative AI is becoming an important medium for artistic creation, yet existing interactions often assume that creators can specify intentions in advance and accurately communicate them through text prompts. Artistic intentions, however, may be vague, latent, or recognizable only after seeing concrete visual possibilities. We propose a human-AI co-creation paradigm beyond explicit intent expression. By expanding model exploration, we expose artists to diverse visual possibilities, allowing them to identify previously unarticulated preferences through observation, comparison, and selection. We then integrate artists' curatorial judgments into reinforcement learning, assigning different learning strengths based on preferences over generation trajectories, so recognized directions are more strongly reinforced and the model gradually adapts to individual aesthetics. This creates a continuous "explore-identify-shape-re-explore" loop in which artistic intent is progressively discovered, externalized, and shaped. kartice.naslov: Unified Multiparadigm Fusion Intelligence for Rare Disease Diagnosis
kartice.povzetek_sl:
arXiv:2610.24024v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rare diseases (RDs) affect an estimated 300 million people globally, leaving patients to navigate a protracted diagnostic odyssey constrained by clinical scarcity and fragmented medical knowledge. Artificial intelligence (AI) has progressively advanced RD diagnostics, from symbolic methods and deep learning to large language model (LLM)-based systems. However, each paradigm carries structural limitations: symbolic methods are bounded by knowledge completeness, neural models sacrifice interpretability, and LLM-based systems are vulnerable to evaluation biases like data leakage. In this study, we introduce FusionRare, a unified multiparadigm fusion framework integrating knowledge-driven symbolic reasoning, deep-learning pattern recognition, case-based patient retrieval, and LLM-based heuristic inference via statistical meta-aggregation and knowledge-enhanced agentic reflection. kartice.naslov: LogicVal:A Logic-Formalized Benchmark for Constraint Satisfaction in Text-to-Image Generation
kartice.povzetek_sl:
arXiv:2610.24051v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Text-to-Image (T2I) generative models have made significant progress in producing high-fidelity images from natural-language prompts. Alongside this progress, numerous benchmarks have been developed to evaluate capabilities such as attribute binding, numeracy, spatial reasoning, and commonsense reasoning. In this work, we propose a new perspective on T2I evaluation by casting it as a constraint-satisfaction problem. We introduce a logical framework that formally specifies the benchmark domain, including objects, attributes, and relations, alongside the constraints that generated images must satisfy. We evaluated four state-of-the-art T2I models across 9 classes of constraints ranging from a single-object-attribute to multi-object relationships constraints involving logical operators ($\forall, \exists, count, \rightarrow$). kartice.naslov: World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds
kartice.povzetek_sl:
arXiv:2610.24061v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As teams of AI agents take on larger projects and long-standing open problems, agent collaboration offers another dimension for scaling inference-time compute. To understand what makes such collaboration effective and scalable, we develop Software World, a framework for simulating multi-agent coworking in realistic software ecosystems. It comes with a pipeline to create environments of real, interdependent Python packages of different topics, sizes, and dependency structures, which we call software worlds. In a simulation, agents maintain packages in the world with a high-level goal of improving software efficiency, and they are free to discover tasks to work on and collaborate with others. We evaluate agents' work in a world collectively by measuring speedup in hidden dependent packages. The framework allows us to study different elements of collaboration by varying communication, ownership, and resource allocation. We run simulations in three different worlds, totaling more than 10,000 hours of agent work across eight models. kartice.naslov: DUET: Decoupled Upper- and Lower-Body Execution for Task-Agnostic Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
kartice.povzetek_sl:
arXiv:2610.23872v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Changing a humanoid robot's manipulation policy should not require retraining the controller that maintains the robot's balance. This study introduces DUET, a decoupled execution framework that enables locomotion and manipulation controllers to operate simultaneously by combining their commands only at the robot interface. A reinforcement-learning locomotion policy controls the 12 leg joints and a waist yaw joint, tracking planar velocity, turning rate, and pelvis height from deep crouching to upright standing on a 23-degree-of-freedom Unitree G1. The 10 arm joints are excluded from the action space, while their positions and velocities are included only as observations, so that any compatible manipulation policy that generates arm-joint targets can control the upper body, and the locomotion policy keeps the lower body stable without requiring shared training or direct coordination. kartice.naslov: Context-Aware RGB-Thermal-Radar Obstacle Perception for Resource-Constrained ASVs
kartice.povzetek_sl:
arXiv:2610.23873v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reliable obstacle perception is challenging for small autonomous surface vessels (ASVs): reflections and glare confound visible-light cameras, vessel motion shifts the apparent waterline, and darkness removes the dominant sensing modality altogether. Rather than treating multimodal fusion as a static accuracy gain, we propose a context-aware architecture that combines RGB and long-wave infrared (LWIR) imagery, frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) mmWave radar, and inertial context. A bearing-sector interface provides the navigation controller with calibrated obstacle probabilities, radar ranges, and sensor status. It also distinguishes sensor dropout from a valid observation with no detected obstacle. Using new multimodal lake recordings, we deployed the pipeline in a 24-leg closed-loop pilot under uncontrolled lake conditions (16 day, 4 dusk, and 4 night; 351 m), including night legs in which RGB was unusable and the vessel drove on LWIR and radar evidence alone. kartice.naslov: Adaptive Question Generation for Ambiguous Robot Instructions Based on Information Gain and Human Cognitive Characteristics
kartice.povzetek_sl:
arXiv:2610.23874v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this study, we propose an adaptive question generation mechanism that addresses uncertainty arising from ambiguous instructions. Natural-language instructions for service robots often contain ambiguities. In scenes with multiple similar objects, the robot must identify the target object by asking questions. However, existing question generation methods focus on probabilistic discrimination efficiency and do not sufficiently account for user ease of response. Asking questions without considering the user's ease of response may cause incorrect or uncertain answers. kartice.naslov: Stress-Query and Temporal Reliability of Vision-Language Models as copilots in Autonomous UAV Navigation
kartice.povzetek_sl:
arXiv:2610.23877v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Integrating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) into autonomous UAV navigation enables high-level semantic reasoning but introduces critical temporal bottlenecks that can destabilize flight control. This paper presents a systematic benchmark that evaluates the operational trade-offs among model scale, hardware constraints, and flight reliability. By subjecting the system to extensive stress tests on both a high-performance workstation and a constrained integrated-graphics laptop, we isolate the kinetic impact of inference latency against reasoning accuracy. Our findings reveal a performance dichotomy: lightweight models struggle with structural hallucinations that break deterministic state machines, while heavyweight models induce trajectory overcorrections due to inference lag. We demonstrate that a mid-weight architecture strikes the optimal balance, successfully rehabilitating navigation in degraded environments without compromising real-time stability across different hardware profiles.

viri.naslov: Stress-Query and Temporal Reliability of Vision-Language Models as copilots in Autonomous UAV Navigation
